newsitem.title: USA: AT&T in transatlantic submarine cable deal.
newsitem.headline: AT&T in transatlantic submarine cable deal.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Monday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with three southern European telecommunication companies to build a transatlantic undersea cable that will go into operation by July 1999.
AT&T's partners are Telefonica de Espana SA of Spain, Telecom Italia SpA of Italy, and Portugal's Companhia Portuguesa Radio Marconi.
The total cost of the project, called Columbus III, is expected to be $270 million to $310 million, AT&T said.
AT&T said Columbus III will help meet explosive demand for communications capacity that has nearly exhausted an existing network, Columbus II.
The four partners are taking equal equity stakes, an AT&T spokeswoman said. No vendors have yet been decided for building the cable system, she said.
AT&T said Friday it was selling AT&T Submarine Systems Inc, which would be one possible vendor for Columbus III, to Tyco International Ltd for $850 million.
Columbus III is expected to span 11,000 kilometers (6,875 miles) in a ring from Florida to the U.S. Virgin islands, Lisbon and the Azores in Portugal, Conil in Spain and Mazara, Italy.
Cancun, Mexico, which is linked into the Columbus II cable, will not be connected to the new cable.
The AT&T spokeswoman said she could not speculate on what would happen to the cable deal if Telefonica, as widely reported, decides to leave AT&T's Unisource European alliance.
Analysts expect Telefonica to announce in the next few weeks that it will join Concert, a global group led by British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp .
